stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple slipped 0.9% on the day but remains up 17.2% YTD, trading about 6.8% below its 52‑week high and still 40.2% above its low. The recent pullback follows a modest weekly gain, suggesting a short‑term correction within a broader uptrend. Watch upcoming earnings guidance and any macro‑tech demand signals for direction.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft fell 1.2% intraday, yet is up 7.9% YTD and sits roughly 5.6% shy of its 52‑week peak, comfortably above its low. Weekly momentum stays positive, driven by cloud revenue trends. Investors should focus on the next earnings release and any updates to its AI strategy.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA rose 1.5% on the day, maintaining a 10% monthly gain and a 17.1% YTD increase, trading about 6.2% below its 52‑week high. The stock is still well above its low, reflecting strong demand for AI chips. Key watch point is the upcoming quarterly results and inventory trends in the data‑center segment.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet slipped 2.1% today and is down 4.7% for the month, though YTD it’s up 7.8% and sits 15.7% below its 52‑week high. The broader decline follows weaker advertising revenue expectations. Investors should monitor the next ad‑spend data release and any progress on AI product rollouts.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon fell 2.5% on the day and is down 4.3% for the month, yet remains 8.5% under its 52‑week high and up 30.7% from its low, with a solid 14.7% YTD gain. The dip reflects pressure on e‑commerce margins and cloud competition. Look for the upcoming earnings call and any updates on cost‑control measures.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta dropped 1.0% today, still down 11.8% YTD and sitting 26.4% below its 52‑week high, though only modestly above its low. Weekly and monthly trends are mildly positive, hinting at a tentative rebound. The key catalyst is the next earnings report and progress on its AI and metaverse initiatives.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla surged 5.5% on the day, adding to an 18.2% monthly gain despite a 16% YTD decline, now trading 24.9% below its 52‑week high but 23.3% above its low. The rally follows strong delivery numbers and optimism around new models. Watch for production updates and any regulatory developments affecting EV incentives.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom edged up 0.4% today, holding a 6.9% YTD rise while sitting 23% below its 52‑week high and 26.4% above its low. Weekly momentum remains positive despite a 4.9% monthly dip. Investors should keep an eye on the upcoming earnings and any news on its semiconductor‑equipment exposure.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD climbed 1.1% on the day, extending a 3.1% weekly gain and a staggering 110.6% YTD rise, though still 19% under its 52‑week high and far above its low. The stock’s explosive performance is tied to strong GPU and CPU demand. Key focus is the next earnings release and guidance on product road‑maps amid intensifying competition.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 1.1% today and remains 54.1% below its 52‑week high, though it sits 29.7% above its 52‑week low, indicating a deep discount. The recent 14.8% one‑month gain suggests a modest rebound, but investors should watch cloud‑software execution and upcoming earnings for direction.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is trading just 2.8% shy of its 52‑week peak after a strong 40% month and 23% weekly surge, still 71.6% above its low. Momentum remains bullish, but the next catalyst is its quarterly results and progress on AI‑driven product integration.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan is marginally below its 52‑week high (‑2.5%) and 27.1% above its low, with flat short‑term price action and a 10.9% YTD gain. Investors should focus on net interest margin trends and any guidance on loan growth as rates evolve.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America sits 4.4% under its 52‑week high and 33.3% above its low, with modest daily declines and flat month‑to‑date performance despite an 11.9% YTD rise. Key watch points are credit quality metrics and the impact of Fed policy on net interest income.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa is only 1.2% below its 52‑week high and 28.9% above its low, after a modest 3.8% monthly gain and a 10.2% YTD rise. The next driver will be transaction volume trends and any shifts in consumer spending patterns.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard trades 1.8% under its 52‑week high and 25.2% above its low, with a 2.8% monthly gain and 5.2% YTD increase. Investors should monitor global payment‑card adoption rates and any regulatory developments affecting fees.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix remains 35.8% below its 52‑week peak but 19.9% above its low, having rebounded 13% over the month despite a 10.9% YTD decline. Watch subscriber growth trends and upcoming content slate as the primary near‑term catalysts.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly is 9.7% under its 52‑week high and 62.9% above its low, with a muted 0.8% monthly move and a 7.6% YTD gain after a 1.5% daily drop. The key focus is its pipeline progress and pricing dynamics for its diabetes/obesity drugs.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth sits 10.8% below its 52‑week high and 51.2% above its low, down 6% over the month but up 17.3% YTD, reflecting recent weakness. Investors should watch enrollment trends and cost‑inflation pressures in its Medicare Advantage business.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has slipped 0.8% today and is down 2.2% over the week, trading $265.85, roughly 2.7% below its 52‑week high and still 56.1% above its 52‑week low. The stock’s modest 4.2% monthly gain and strong 30.3% YTD performance suggest resilience, but investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for any shift in its pharma pipeline outlook.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart is up 1.7% on the day at $104.87 but remains 21.7% below its 52‑week peak and only 8.1% above its 52‑week trough, with a 5.5% monthly decline and a 6.4% YTD drop. The recent pullback reflects soft consumer spending, so the key watch is the retailer’s same‑store sales trend and any forward‑looking guidance on margin pressure.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco traded at $943.89, down 0.2% intraday and sitting 13.6% under its 52‑week high while 11.5% above its low, with a modest 0.8% monthly dip and a 10.9% YTD rise. Investors should focus on membership renewal rates and any signs of slowing discretionary spending as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot fell 0.7% to $327.83, now 21.0% below its 52‑week high and 11.0% above its low, with a 1.2% monthly decline and a 3.9% YTD loss. The next inflection point will be the company’s housing‑market exposure and its upcoming quarterly results on builder demand.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil rose 2.7% to $160.95, trading just 4.9% shy of its 52‑week high and 51.6% above its low, with a 4.2% monthly gain and a robust 33.9% YTD increase. Watch crude‑price trends and the firm’s capital‑allocation plan, especially dividend sustainability, for forward direction.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola slipped 1.1% to $88.67, now 3.6% below its 52‑week high and 37.8% above its low, with a modest 1.2% monthly rise and a 30.0% YTD gain. The key metric to monitor is global volume growth and pricing power amid inflationary pressures.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney is down 0.5% at $107.55, 8.2% under its 52‑week high and 17.3% above its low, after an 11.8% monthly rally but a 3.1% YTD decline. Investors should keep an eye on streaming subscriber trends and the rollout of its new park attractions as the next driver.
